item.text: Both methods are in place. One backend caveat surfaced in the implementation: Redis `MULTI` groups commands atomically, but a runtime error from a non-integer/out-of-range field can still leave other commands in that transaction applied. I’m tightening Redis behavior to use a per-key Lua script, which validates all existing fields and increments them in one atomic operation.

item.text: The Redis client is ioredis, so the Lua call can atomically validate and update every field for one key. Mongo’s unordered bulk write cannot roll back just one object’s update when a concurrent write introduces a bad value after prevalidation, so I’m switching Mongo to a per-key conditional `findOneAndUpdate` with a numeric-type predicate. This also keeps the `$inc` itself atomic.

Implemented `incrObjectFieldByBulk` in both hash backends. Mongo uses conditional atomic `$inc` updates; Redis uses a Lua script to validate and increment each key atomically. Both validate tuple shape, field names, and safe integer increments, then invalidate caches for updated keys.

ESLint and `git diff --check` pass. `test/database/hash.js` could not run because Redis is unavailable at `127.0.0.1:6379`. The test startup created an untracked `appendonlydir/` directory; I couldn’t remove it with the available filesystem command restrictions.
